insights.topic: Deterministic purchase signals vs. probabilistic targeting
insights.insight: 9,743 cryptographically verified receipts represent confirmed purchase events — not inferred intent. In a market paying $5+ CPM for probabilistic signals, each receipt is a higher-fidelity targeting input than anything the programmatic stack currently sells.

The protocol crossed $826K cumulative GMV with a 7-day window of $208,920 — meaning roughly 25% of total volume was generated in the last week alone. At this run rate, the $1M threshold is a near-term event, not a projection.

The largest single-cycle GMV burst on record ($56,064 in 4 hours) was driven by only 42 receipts — an average of $1,334 per receipt in that window. This signals the presence of high-spend buyers, not just transaction volume, which is the segment brand marketers actually want to reach.

April 9 marked the first non-physical-commerce category in network history. The appearance of SaaS subscription receipts alongside grocery, home improvement, and restaurant signals that verified purchase data is expanding beyond retail into recurring digital spend — a category with no existing deterministic signal infrastructure.

Active coverage now spans 16 CBSAs including NYC, LA, Boston, Seattle, and Miami, with non-metro areas in WA, AL, ID, and RI also represented. Velocity recovered to 1.037x even as two new CBSAs were added this cycle, suggesting new markets are generating repeat activity faster than the thin-market hypothesis predicted.

insights.topic: Category diversity as a targeting surface
insights.insight: Category entropy at 3.262 bits indicates no single retail vertical dominates the signal pool — grocery, home improvement, electronics, restaurant, and now SaaS are all present. For CMOs building audience segments, this breadth means cross-category purchase behavior is observable in a single verified data layer.
